standard_prerequisites.name: In an extension of discrete valuation rings every uniformizer of the smaller ring is a unit multiple of a power of a uniformizer of the larger ring, and the exponent is the ramification index
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof line 32973, where pi_A = u pi_B^e is written with u in the units of B
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the first of the two valuations to be compared.

standard_prerequisites.name: If L over K is purely inseparable of characteristic p, then a power of every element of L lies in K, in particular a p-power power of pi_B lies in K
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 32974-32975, where pi_B^q is placed in K for some p-power q and then written as v pi_A^k
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the second valuation equation whose exponent k is determined by the valuation of pi_B^q, namely k = q/e.

standard_prerequisites.name: Valuations of an extension of discrete valuation rings are multiplicative and take the value zero exactly on units, so equalities of elements up to units give equalities of valuations
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 32976-32977, where taking valuations in B of pi_A^q = u^q v^e pi_A^{ke} gives ke = q
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the two writings of the same element into the numerical relation ke = q, hence e divides a power of p.

core_obligations: Write pi_A = u pi_B^e for some unit u of B, which records that the ramification index e relates the two chosen uniformizers (proof line 32973).
Use pure inseparability of L over K to find a p-power q with pi_B^q in K, and write pi_B^q = v pi_A^k with v a unit of A and k an integer (proof lines 32974-32975).
Substitute the two writings into each other: pi_A^q = u^q pi_B^{qe} = u^q v^e pi_A^{ke}, so that the two expressions for the same element differ by the unit u^q v^e (proof line 32976).

Take valuations in B and use multiplicativity to conclude ke = q; since q is a power of p and e is a positive integer dividing q, the ramification index is a power of p, which is the assertion of the lemma (proof lines 32976-32977).
proof_roadmap: Relate the two uniformizers by writing pi_A as a unit times pi_B^e (proof line 32973).
Use pure inseparability to bring a p-power of pi_B into K and write it as a unit times pi_A^k (proof lines 32974-32975).
Compare the two writings after substitution and take valuations in B to obtain ke = q, whence e is a power of p (proof lines 32976-32977).
difficulty_reason: The statement is a numerical restriction on ramification in characteristic p: for an extension of discrete valuation rings A contained in B inducing K contained in L with K of characteristic p and L purely inseparable over K, the ramification index e is a power of p (statement lines 32964-32970). The proof is short and explicit: it writes pi_A as a unit times pi_B^e, uses pure inseparability to place a p-power of pi_B in K and hence to write that power as a unit times pi_A^k, substitutes the two expressions into one another, and takes valuations in B to obtain the relation ke = q with q a power of p (proof lines 32973-32977). The point is not the length of the computation but that the two unit writings conflate into a single numerical equation, which is what forces the divisibility conclusion. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.
